players.product: ultra-high-purity carrier gases and electronic specialty gases

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 2026 group comparable sales growth was +3.5%, a pickup from +1.9% in Q1; Q2 sales growth excluding currency and energy pass-through was +5.2%, including the scope effect of the DIG Airgas acquisition net of the biogas divestiture. H1 2026 comparable growth was +2.6%; currency was a -3.6% headwind and the DIG Airgas scope effect +1.7%. Americas grew +5% comparable in Q2. CEO: growth was driven by booming electronics and improving industrial merchants.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 comparable +3.5% (Q1 +1.9%); Q2 +5.2% excl. FX and energy; H1 comparable +2.6%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Electronics sales growth accelerated to +10% in Q2 as prior-year equipment and installation comparables rolled off, driven by carrier gas startups and ramp-ups mainly in China and Taiwan and broad-based momentum in advanced materials (Air Liquide's proprietary molecules). One South Korean customer pulled a Q3 order forward after the legal and IT merger of DIG Airgas and Air Liquide Korea; normalised for this, underlying Electronics growth was +8%. CEO: some customers are catching up with advanced purchases of advanced materials.

CEO: 'we do expect electronics to remain in the range of 8%, maybe 9% for the rest of the year.' CFO: the company confirms its guidance for 2026 and 2027, cumulating a +560 bps margin improvement over a six-year period.
quarterly_data.figure: electronics growth 8%, maybe 9% for rest of 2026; +560 bps cumulative margin improvement

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: H1 2026 group margin expanded +110 basis points excluding energy pass-through and the DIG Airgas PPA impact (+100 bps including PPA); Americas margin rose +200 bps versus H1 2025. Efficiencies reached a record EUR 299 million in H1 (+4%). Industrial merchant pricing was +5.2% in Q2 (CEO), with Americas +6.7%, EMEA +3.1% and Asia +1.4% (from -0.4% in Q1). Recurring net profit group share was EUR 1.9 billion, +4.4% as published and +10% at constant currency; recurring ROCE 11%.
quarterly_data.figure: margin +110 basis points; efficiencies EUR 299 million; recurring net profit EUR 1.9 billion (+10% constant currency); ROCE 11%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: electronics project decisions reached over EUR 1 billion in H1 2026, one and a half times the total for all 2025, almost all driven by artificial intelligence needs. In the U.S. the company secured three large-scale projects in H1 with a total investment of over $480 million, all dedicated to advanced chips with leading semiconductor manufacturers (unnamed); project signings in Asia totaled more than EUR 550 million. CEO: Air Liquide's investment in new fabs grew 146% in the first semester, 'much ahead of the industry'; current sales reflect the production of current fabs, and new investments contribute to sales in two, three, four years depending on size.
quarterly_data.figure: over EUR 1 billion electronics decisions; over $480 million (3 U.S. projects); more than EUR 550 million in Asia; 146%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: investment backlog of signed projects under execution reached a record EUR 6 billion (EUR 5.5 billion in Q1 2026), up +30% year-over-year; CEO: 40% of the backlog is electronics. Industrial investment decisions hit an all-time high EUR 2.9 billion in H1 2026 (+26%). The 12-month investment opportunity portfolio reached EUR 4.8 billion (+17%), nearly 80 projects, electronics about 50%; the total portfolio including beyond 12 months exceeds EUR 10 billion. CEO: significant startups in Q3 and Q4 will draw the backlog down, so it is expected to remain more or less flat.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog EUR 6 billion (+30%); 40% electronics; decisions EUR 2.9 billion; 12-month portfolio EUR 4.8 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: the global helium supply chain remains a point of attention; Qatar production restarted at limited/reduced capacity and Air Liquide secured some volume, while Q2 also saw restrictions on Russian product to China and out of China. The helium shortage weighed on merchant volumes. CFO: electronics customers are supplied under long-term contracts and helium is 'in no means a limitation' to the electronics business; the company uses its storage cavern and multiple other sources, but stays 'extremely cautious' as the situation is fluid.

VP North America Adam Peters: gas intensity is higher in new fabs supporting advanced chips for high bandwidth memory or AI logic; Air Liquide has very active discussions with all the major players on U.S. expansions and new projects. CEO by region: Japan 'is waking up' with government support and Air Liquide is the only global international gas company there; Taiwan is extremely dynamic for the most advanced chips; in Korea the DIG Airgas acquisition positions it to meet the needs of the leading memory players building mega campuses; China, where it holds a number one electronics position, is very dynamic. CEO: signed projects are mid-size to large, not extra-large, but the company may position itself on some very large projects in the future.

CEO: three major large-industries projects signed in H1: a $350 million investment under a new long-term agreement to supply air gases to Hyundai POSCO's low-carbon steel plants in Louisiana; a $200 million new plant producing low-carbon syngas and hydrogen at Oxea's Bay City, Texas site; and a EUR 70 million investment to supply nitrogen to Silleno's polyethylene facility in Kazakhstan. VP EMEA: the Normandy electrolyzer will start up this year and is fully loaded.

connects_to.relationship: electronics carrier gas projects in the U.S. and South Korea

contracts.signal: CEO: following the DIG Airgas acquisition in Korea, Air Liquide further leveraged its global relationship with key players like SK hynix, with project wins both in the U.S. and in South Korea (part of over EUR 1 billion of H1 2026 electronics project decisions).
